<reason>Both sides built coherent, well-executed cases and directly engaged the pressure round (A1/A2, Q1/Q2 formats were properly honored). B's opening was rhetorically compelling — the "tell" argument, the three harms (extraction, unaccountable proxies, corrosion of market signals), and the eventual dilemma fork ("if it survives disclosure it was fine; if it dies, it was never a real subsidy") gave PRO a clean, memorable frame. But A's verification-gate rebuttal (A2.1-A2.3) was the debate's pivot: unlike student/senior discounts, algorithmic criteria cannot be gated, so disclosing them hands sophisticated buyers the exact signal to spoof, manufacturing the very collapse PRO later blames on illegitimacy rather than mechanism. PRO's counter (the "swap test" plus aggregate/after-the-fact disclosure) was a smart attempt to preserve enforceability without publishing gameable criteria, but A's fingerprinting-filtering rebuttal and the closing reframe of the fork ("naming the criteria teaches everyone how to claim it — that's disclosure manufacturing the collapse, not unmasking a fake discount") were left substantially standing. A also successfully turned B's own "unsophisticated buyers are trapped" harm into a wash by showing that group already pays the most regardless of the rule, and B's closing reply ("that's the status quo you're defending") was rhetorically resonant but didn't rebut the causal claim. A's clipped Rebuttal 1 (word-limit format note) is a real execution cost for B, and A held the final word cleanly resolving the central fork. The debate was close and well-matched, but A's mechanism-level rebuttals did more actual damage to PRO's core dilemma than PRO's rebuttals did to CON's ratchet theory.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's verification-gate rebuttal (A2.1-A2.3), distinguishing gated public discounts from ungateable algorithmic criteria, which reframed the entire ratchet-vs-dilemma clash for the rest of the debate and was never fully neutralized by PRO's swap-test/aggregate-disclosure fix.</best_rebuttal>
